doc.spoiler_a11y_desc: The toggle is a native <button> carrying aria-expanded for the current state and aria-controls pointing to the clamped region, so assistive technologies announce both the action and its target. The clamped text is hidden visually by overflow, not removed from the accessibility tree, so screen readers can always read the full content. Focus stays on the toggle across expand and collapse, keeping the keyboard position stable.
doc.spoiler_best_practice_1: Let the component decide whether the toggle is needed instead of tracking text length yourself — the overflow check already accounts for container width, font size, and translations.
doc.spoiler_best_practice_2: Use the controlled expanded prop when the state must be shared (for example, an "expand all reviews" action or persisting the state per item); otherwise prefer the simpler uncontrolled default.
doc.spoiler_best_practice_3: Avoid nesting interactive elements near the clamp edge: a link that ends up half-hidden on the clamped line is still focusable but not fully readable. Keep links and buttons in the always-visible part or at the start of the text.
doc.spoiler_choice_accordion_when: When hiding and revealing titled sections of arbitrary content, such as FAQ entries or settings groups, where each section has a header.
doc.spoiler_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on what is being collapsed:
doc.spoiler_choice_scrollarea_when: When the full content must stay reachable inside a fixed-height region and scrolling is preferable to expanding the page.
doc.spoiler_choice_self_when: When a single block of running text (review, comment, product description, bio) should be previewed by line count and expanded in place.
doc.spoiler_content_guideline_1: Keep the toggle labels short and outcome-oriented ("Show more" / "Show less"). Avoid vague labels like "More" that could be read as a navigation link.
doc.spoiler_content_guideline_2: Choose a collapsed line count that preserves a meaningful preview — usually 2 to 5 lines. A one-line preview of a long review rarely gives users enough signal to decide whether to expand.
doc.spoiler_default_expanded_desc: defaultExpanded renders the full text initially while keeping the toggle so users can collapse it. Use the expanded prop instead for fully controlled state.
doc.spoiler_design_intent: Long user-generated text competes with everything else on the page: a feed of full-length reviews buries the content around it, while hard truncation hides information with no way back. Clamping to a line count (rather than a pixel height) keeps the cut point aligned with the text grid at any font size, and letting the component decide whether a toggle is needed removes the most common failure of hand-rolled implementations: a dangling "show more" under text that already fits.
doc.spoiler_i18n_desc: The default toggle labels use the spoiler.show_more and spoiler.show_less translation keys, shipped in en / ja / pt, and follow the current i18next language. Pass showLabel / hideLabel to override them per instance; the clamped body text itself is consumer content.
doc.spoiler_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus to the toggle button; Enter and Space activate it, as with any native button. Focus remains on the toggle after expanding or collapsing, so repeated activation toggles the state without re-orienting.
doc.spoiler_labels_desc: showLabel and hideLabel replace the built-in localized labels, for example to name the content ("Read full review").
doc.spoiler_lines_desc: The lines prop sets how many lines remain visible while collapsed. The value is injected as a CSS custom property, so it adapts to any font size or container width.
doc.spoiler_long_desc: Spoiler truncates reviews, comments, and other long text to a configurable number of lines using CSS line-clamp, and reveals the rest through a toggle button wired with aria-expanded and aria-controls. The toggle appears only when the text actually overflows the collapsed height (re-checked via ResizeObserver on resize and content changes), and the clamped text stays in the DOM so screen readers and in-page search still see the full content.
doc.spoiler_motion_desc: No animation is applied: expanding swaps the line-clamp off and the content takes its natural height in one step. Because the reveal is user-initiated and adjacent content only moves downward, an instant transition is predictable and needs no prefers-reduced-motion handling.
doc.spoiler_prop_defaultExpanded: Initial expanded state for uncontrolled usage.
doc.spoiler_prop_expanded: Controlled expanded state. Use together with onExpandedChange.
doc.spoiler_prop_hideLabel: Label of the toggle while expanded. Defaults to the localized "Show less".
doc.spoiler_prop_lines: Number of text lines shown while collapsed.
doc.spoiler_prop_onExpandedChange: Called with the next state when the toggle is activated.
doc.spoiler_prop_showLabel: Label of the toggle while collapsed. Defaults to the localized "Show more".
doc.spoiler_responsive_desc: The clamp is line-based, so the same lines value produces a consistent preview at any container width; the overflow check re-runs via ResizeObserver when the container resizes, showing or hiding the toggle as the text reflows. No breakpoint-specific handling is needed.
doc.spoiler_rich_desc: Children are not limited to plain strings; nested markup such as paragraphs and inline emphasis is clamped as a whole.
doc.spoiler_scenario_1: Clamp each review in a list to 3 lines so users can scan many opinions quickly and expand only the ones worth reading in full.
doc.spoiler_scenario_2: Collapse long comments in discussions and activity feeds; short replies render without a toggle, so the thread stays visually uniform.
doc.spoiler_scenario_3: Show the first lines of a long description above the fold and let interested users expand it without navigating away from the purchase actions.
doc.spoiler_short_desc: When the text fits within the line limit, no toggle is rendered — lists mixing short and long entries stay clean without extra logic.
doc.spoiler_title: Collapse long text to a fixed number of lines with an accessible "show more" toggle.
